title: Extract and deduplicate free-text entries using a synonym dictionary
when_to_use: When the task requires analyzing distributions or frequencies from unstructured text fields like job descriptions or benefits.
experience:
- Identify all relevant columns that may contain target entities (e.g., `Benefits`, `Job Description`).
- Extract all unique text entries from those columns and manually review a sample to understand variations.
- Create a synonym mapping table that groups semantically equivalent entries (e.g., 'Five social insurances', 'Five insurances and one housing fund' → 'social insurance').
- Apply the mapping to standardize entries before counting frequencies or calculating percentages.
- Validate the deduplication by checking that the total count of original entries matches the sum of counts per standardized category.
- Report both the raw extracted list and the grouped distribution, noting the mapping rules used.
checklist: Identify all source columns containing free-text data
Review sample entries to spot synonyms and variations
Build a synonym dictionary for standardization
Apply dictionary to clean and group entries
Verify counts before and after grouping
common_failure_prevented: Incomplete or inaccurate distribution analysis due to not merging synonymous entries (e.g., benefits listed differently).

title: Define and apply explicit thresholds for statistical significance
when_to_use: When the task requires identifying which factors 'significantly' increase an outcome like salary.
experience:
- Before analysis, define what 'significant' means: e.g., minimum sample size (e.g., count >=5), minimum effect size (e.g., salary lift >=500 RMB), or statistical test (e.g., t-test p-value <0.05).
- Compute the outcome metric (e.g., average starting salary) for each factor level and also for the baseline (e.g., factor not mentioned).
- Calculate the lift (difference or percentage change) between factor-present and baseline groups.
- Apply the predefined thresholds to filter factors: only report those meeting both sample size and effect size criteria.
- If using statistical tests, ensure assumptions (e.g., normality, equal variance) are checked or use non-parametric alternatives.
- In the conclusion, explicitly state the thresholds used and how many factors passed them.
checklist: Define thresholds for sample size and effect size/statistical test
common_failure_prevented: Reporting factors as 'significant' based on arbitrary or implicit criteria rather than robust, defined rules.

title: Use keyword extraction from unstructured text to complement structured fields
when_to_use: When the task requires analyzing qualities, skills, or attributes that may be embedded in free-text descriptions.
experience:
- Identify all unstructured text columns (e.g., `Job Description`, `Requirements`) that may contain relevant information not captured in structured fields.
- Define a comprehensive keyword list for each category of interest (e.g., certificates: 'certificate', 'license', 'qualification'; soft skills: 'communication', 'teamwork').
- Use case‑insensitive pattern matching (including common synonyms and abbreviations) to flag rows containing each keyword.
- Count occurrences per keyword and per category, and compute associated outcome metrics (e.g., average salary for rows mentioning each keyword).
- Validate extraction by manually reviewing a random sample of flagged rows to check precision.
- Report results alongside structured field analysis, noting the source column and extraction method.
checklist: Build keyword lists for each category of interest
Validate extraction precision with manual review
common_failure_prevented: Missing important factors because they were only mentioned in free‑text descriptions and not in structured columns.
